treatment_label: AC Shoulder Restoration, Asphalt Concrete Overlay, Partial depth patching of PCC pavements at joints
short_interpretation: This Wisconsin corridor case shows a major treatment event on route 2_43 with a very large drop in treated-node cracking and a strong simultaneous decline across many graph neighbours. It is a good illustration of how graph-linked sections can move together after a corridor-scale intervention.
limitations_caution: The treatment label bundles several activities together, so the effect cannot be attributed to a single treatment component. This is a strong corridor case study, but not a clean single-treatment causal example.

short_interpretation: This Missouri case represents a heavier rehabilitation-style event involving subdrain work. The treated section improves sharply and neighbouring sections also show substantial reductions in cracking, which makes it useful for discussing broader network or corridor spillover.
limitations_caution: The route label is missing, which makes the corridor visually less intuitive than the Wisconsin example. The event is also infrastructure-heavy, so it may capture multiple mechanisms beyond surface distress treatment.

treatment_label: Grinding Surface, Full Depth Transverse Joint Repair Patch, Joint Load Transfer Restoration in PCC Pavements
short_interpretation: This Ohio case offers a more focused route-labelled example involving grinding and repair patching on route 2_71. It is visually useful in a dissertation demo because the route context is clear, even though the neighbour sample is small.
limitations_caution: Only one neighbour had usable pre/post data, so this is best treated as a compact illustrative example rather than strong evidence of neighbour propagation.
